description: Message IDs, cursors, has_more, SSE, text-delta, attribution, handoff, Direct Conversations, closure, and errors.

cases.description: Starting a conversation returns 201 with conversation_id; every read has cursor, has_more, working, handoff, responder, closed; company messages have author (§8.3, §8.7).
Sending the same request (same ID, same path, same body) again returns the original response and adds nothing (§8.3).
Reusing a request ID with a different body, or at another path, is request_id_conflict (409) (§8.3).
A cursor the company never issued is invalid_cursor (400).
A cursor for forgotten events is cursor_expired (410); the SDK reads from the beginning and tells the host part is missing.
With more events than a page, has_more is true and the SDK drains every page in order without duplicates.
A read with nothing new returns no events, the request's cursor, has_more false, and the state fields working, handoff, responder and closed.
Every successful read includes conversation_id, events (empty when there are none), cursor, has_more, and the state fields working, handoff, responder and closed.
A stream reopened with Last-Event-ID resumes after the last handled event, without repeating it.
text-delta pieces arrive as non-actionable display text; only the complete message event carries the reply.
The user's own words go as author human and come back with role user; company messages carry role company and an author.

A company agent message's as_of_request, when present, names a request the agent sent; a person's message carries neither as_of_request nor as_of_cursor, and the agent's own as_of_cursor comes back as sent (§8.4).
A handoff is accepted (202); handoff is pending while a person is looked for, and a state event records each change of handoff, responder or closed (§8.7, §8.9).
A handoff cancel is accepted (202); the company stops looking or a person joined first, read from handoff and responder; a cancel with nothing pending changes nothing (§8.9).
A Direct Conversation names its parent; the parent gets direct_opened, refuses messages with direct_conversation_open, and gets direct_closed when it closes.
A Direct Conversation cannot be the parent of another: invalid_request.
A signed-out question gets an authorization event (and a message saying so); after sign-in the same conversation continues with the new token.
A close is accepted (202) and, once acted on, closed is true with a state event; a later message or handoff cancel is conversation_closed (409), a close again 202; the events stay readable (§8.12).
An unknown conversation and another user's conversation give the same conversation_not_found (404) body.
Once a conversation used the account, a signed-out token for the same user gets insufficient_scope.
